## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical equipment problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running without hydraulic load, indicating a mechanical failure or disconnection. All other components are in good condition, but the pump failure prevents normal system operation and poses a risk of motor damage from overheating.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The tank liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Parameter | Measured | Nameplate | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amp Draw | 1.6 A | 7.2 A | CRITICAL - No Load |

The pump is running at 22.2% of full load amperage. This indicates the pump motor is operating without hydraulic load -- the pump is spinning but not moving fluid. The high water alarm tested functional and electrical connections are sound, ruling out control circuit failure. The probable causes are a broken or missing impeller, a severed or disconnected discharge line, or a dry-run condition. Motor damage from overheating without fluid cooling is a real risk if operation continues.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no visible breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**CRITICAL - Immediate professional attention required:**
The effluent pump is operating without hydraulic load. Do not continue operating the system until the pump discharge line is inspected for disconnection or blockage, and the pump impeller is inspected for damage or failure. Continued operation risks permanent motor damage.

**Routine:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once pump operation is restored and verified.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a mechanical problem inside the pump or in the discharge line that connects it to the dispersal field. The pump motor can overheat and burn out if it runs dry for an extended period. Do not delay in having a technician inspect and repair the pump and discharge line. Until the pump is repaired, the system cannot treat and disperse wastewater properly.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Solids will continue to accumulate over time. Keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications -- to keep that accumulation predictable and slow.
